newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Two killed in Nigerian political party primaries.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Nigerian political party primaries.

text.p: Two Nigerians died when supporters of two potential candidates for local council polls clashed, newspapers reported on Tuesday.
They said the clash took place on Monday in the central Nigerian city of Jos and that in at least two other wards in the vast West African nation there were scuffles.
Those killed were supporters of two Congress for National Consensus (CNC) party aspirants in Jos where the clashes left many vehicles destroyed and a popular restaurant burnt.
Riot police had restored order, Thisday newspaper said, adding that the clash in Jos stemmed from long-standing rivalry between local people and the settler Hausas from further north.
The five registered parties on Monday held congresses in more than 8,000 wards nationwide to choose candidates for local council elections on March 15.
It is part of a transition to civil rule planned by military ruler General Sani Abacha who says the phased polls will lead to his handover of power to an elected president next year.

Nigeria plunged into crisis in 1993. The army annulled a presidential poll to restore democracy and supporters of Moshood Abiola, who is believed to have won that poll, remain critical of Abacha's transition programme and say it will fail.
